Major refactoring to match future MRtrix 3.1.0

- Divide the code across multiple source files.
- Move source files to new location according to MRtrix 3.1.0 filesystem arrangement.

- Perform gradient non-linearity distortion correction if the requisite deformation field is made available.

Modifications to better handle monopolar DWIs

If the input DWIs are detected as having been acquired using a single-refocused diffusion sequence:
- If no images in fmap/ directory, then rather than allowing dwifslpreproc to extract all b=0 volumes from the input DWIs for use in inhomogeneity field map estimation, explicitly extract only those b=0 volumes prior to the first DWI in each input series, as any b=0 volumes subsequent to this may be contaminated by residual eddy currents from previous DWI volumes.
- Instruct eddy to perform linear registration of b=0 volumes rather than rigid-body, since later b=0 volumes may be affected by eddy currents arising from previous DWIs.

Prevent forcing script into container mode

Fix complex DWI import PE

On import of complex DWI data, the import of JSON data needs to occur in the same mrconvert call as where the NIfTI image is loaded. If an mrcalc call is first performed to combine magnitude and phase components, and then mrconvert is used to bring in the JSON information, then the phase encoding direction will not be appropriately rotated when MRtrix3 re-arranges the spatial axes to RAS.
Also sort input DWIs and fmap/ images, so that if volumes have been extracted from the input DWIs and fed to fmap/, then the first volume input to topup is more likely to correspond to the first input volume to eddy.
Also retain dwifslpreproc scratch directory if MRtrix3_connectome is being run with -nocleanup.

Fix identification of FSL flirt executable for Craddock parcellations

Also various comments throughout the script regarding pending modifications.

No longer concatenate dwi/ and fmap/ data

Previously, the script would concatenate all data in the dwi/ and fmap/ directories together prior to running dwidenoise / mrdegibbs. This placed limitations on such images being defined on a common grid, and it may not be ideal from the perspective of denoising to be concatenating data with different phase encoding directions beforehand. With this change, DWI series are denoised independently, and all DWI and fmap/ series have Gibbs ringing removal applied independently. Finally, if it is not possible to directly concatenate all fmap/ data together prior to dwipreproc, all fmap/ images will be resampled onto the voxel grid of the DWIs in preparation for dwipreproc.

Major restructure for dev_3.0.0 branch

- There are now two separate participant-level analyses. "participant1" deals with "pre-processing" for which the end output is pre-processed DWI data and a DWI brain mask that are aligned to the T1-weighted image (for which a bias-field-corrected output and a brain mask are also provided. "participant2" deals with all participant-level analysis for connectome construction beyond that point.

- participant1:
  - Handle input complex data for which the input phase image is not in radians.
  - Perform an iterative approach to multi-tissue-based bias field correction, intensity normalisation, and brain masking, such that the output pre-processed DWI is bias field corrected and has a CSF b=0 intensity of 1000.
  - Perform transformation of the DWI data to align with the T1-weighted image rather than the other way around, since the latter is more likely to form the reference space for many processing pipelines.
  - Flag output DWI as "_desc-preproc", consistently with other BIDS Apps and to prevent file name ambiguity between raw and derived data.

- participant2:
  - Don't generate FA or mean b=0 images; the calculations of these are deferred to group-level analysis.
  - Don't use a dilated brain mask for CSD; just run without a mask at all. The DWI brain mask can always be adopted manually if the user wishes to use these data for manual interaction, but for automated analysis it is safer to not mask at all and instead rely on T1-weighted image processing and ACT for constraint.

- group:
  - Better use of string constants to ensure appropriate referencing of scratch directory paths.
  - Calculate mean b=0 image and FA image during subject import, rather than soft-linking from existing derivative outputs.
  - Use responsemean script rather than doing a direct ZSH coefficient averaging.

Added math_msvc_compatibility.h

MSVC++ 9 has a very outdated definition of <math.h>.
That is why math_msvc_compatibility.h should be imported
(if and only if _MSC_VER is defined).

M_PI is only defined by <math.h> when _USE_MATH_DEFINES
is defined.

isnan, isinf, isfinite are not defined in <math.h>.
Instead, _isnan and _finite must be used.

Furthermore, <math.h> defines copysign as a macro, which
interferes with some macro-heavy code in numpy_quaternion.c.
This is why the wrapper functions are defined as static
inline functions rather than macros.

Add INCREFs to inplace operators [closes #20]

Apparently, the inplace operators decref the return value, rather than
leaving it alone.  I would expect a line like

    a *= b

to have no effect on the reference count of `a`.  Evidently, I was
wrong.  The function would return just fine, and the first use of `a`
would be fine because the stale memory was still being found and used.
But that typically overwrites the memory with a string or something,
so later uses would go haywire.

I've added Py_INCREF to each return from the inplace C
functions, and checked that there is no memory leak using `mprof`.

```bash
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jax_md import space, partition

pos = jnp.array([[0.0, 0.0]])
box_size = jnp.array([1.0,  1.0])
cell_size = 0.1

displacement_fn, shift_fn = space.periodic(box_size)
neighbor_list_fn = partition.neighbor_list(
    displacement_fn, box_size, cell_size, format=partition.Sparse)

print('First iteration neighbor allocation')
_ = neighbor_list_fn.allocate(pos)
print('Second iteration neighbor allocation')
_ = neighbor_list_fn.allocate(pos)
```

```bash

Second iteration neighbor allocation
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/artur/code/jaxmdQF/test.py", line 15, in <module>
    _ = neighbor_list_fn.allocate(pos)
  File "/home/artur/code/jaxmdQF/jax-md/jax_md/partition.py", line 981, in allocate_fn
    return neighbor_list_fn(position, extra_capacity=extra_capacity, **kwargs)

    return neighbor_fn((position, PartitionError(jnp.zeros((), jnp.uint8))))
```

- Release 1.3.0
- Fixed FutureWarning issue with destag routine (thank you honnorat!)
- Fixed computational problems with updraft_helicity, and values are no longer
  scaled by 1000.
- Removed version constraints for wrapt and setuptools.
- Fixed xarray being a hard dependency.
- Fixed unit issues with vinterp when pressure values are extracted below
  ground. Also added support for height fields in km and pressure fields in
  hPa. The documentation has been improved.
- Fixed the smooth2d routine so that it actually works. It never worked
  correctly before (nor did it work in NCL). Users can now specify the
  center weight of the kernel and the documentation has been updated to
  describe how it works.
- Fixed the storm relative helicity algorithm so that it works in the southern
  hemisphere. The raw algorithm now requires latitude input if used
  in the southern hemisphere, otherwise the northern hemisphere is assumed.
- Fixed an issue with the latest version of cartopy 0.17 (thanks honnorat!)
- Fixed an issue where invalid keyword arguments weren't throwing errors when
  extracting standard WRF variables.
- Fixed minor issues related to moving nests when using line interpolation and
  vertical cross sections. It is still an error to request all times when
  using lat/lon coordinates with a moving nest, but otherwise knows how to
  run when all times are requested. This never really worked quite right.
- Removed the pyf file from setup.py since it is generated via the build
  system.
- Added an autolevels parameter for the vertical cross section so that users
  can specify the number of vertical levels to use if they don't want to
  specify them manually.
- The interplevel routine has been improved. Users can now specify a single
  level, multiple levels, or a 2D array (e.g. PBLH) to interpolate to.
  Performance has been improved when interpolating a multiple product
  field like wspd_wdir.
- Products that produce multiple outputs can now have the outputs requested
  individually. See :ref:`subdiagnostic-table` for a list of what is available.
- Much of this version of wrf-python has been back ported to NCL in the
  upcoming 6.6.0 release. The diagnostics should produce the same results
  in both packages.
- Now released under the Apache 2.0 license.

Fix controller_patience when controller_max_retries is -1

When controller_max_retries is -1, the parameter controller_patience
does not have any effect. The controller is stuck in an infinite loop.

The issue is that setVelocityCmd() keeps setting the
getLastValidCmdVelTime() time to ros::Time::now(). This leads to the
patience code never triggering.

The commit 68664fd7a79d1a7ad035b194ce3e6e1ab7fff8fa has introduced this
bug. This commit moves the two lines back to their original location.

Fix race condition between finishing and updating a goal

AbstractActionBase sets slot.in_use to false after having left runImpl.
This means that a check based on slot.in_use might still see a thread as
running despite the goal got assigned a terminal state.
Hence, we also check that the goal is still active to consume an update.

RFC: Prevent actions from deeply queuing for a concurrency slot

While the previous commit prevents memory corruption caused by running a
plugin before the previous (canceled) action completes, it does not prevent
a waiting action from starting the plugin even though the client may have
already canceled.

As a result, if external code starts and cancels an action repeatedly in rapid
succession, all of them are run sequentially even though many of these actions
were already canceled.

This commit contains a partial fix:
If a new action is being started while one is already running in the same
concurrency slot, put it in a "pending" map indexed by slot, then tell the
existing plugin to cancel and wait for it to exit. After waiting, double check
that the current goal ID is still in the pending list before starting the
action plugin. If it's not, mark this goal as canceled and return.

Meanwhile, if the action client cancels a goal that is in the pending list,
remove it therefrom so that .start() will see that it is no longer pending as
described above and will not start the plugin.

FIXME:
While this does prevent the many actions that were already canceled by client code
from continuing to start long after they were canceled, it does so at the
expense of blocking the AbstractAction::start(), which is running on a "goal
callback" from an ActionServer. Since there are a limited number of threads
available for these and all ROS message callbacks, these can fill up, causing
errors such as the costmap not receiving sensor messages.

A proper fix will record pending actions to be processed by a worker queue and
will remove queued items when canceled without blocking the ActionServer
goal_cb.

Makes canceling of already-running plugin thread-safe

When a new action goal is received on the same concurrency slot for which an
action was already running, the existing action was being canceled, but the
it did not wait for this to complete before starting a new one which, as noted
by a comment in the code, is not thread safe. Now it waits for the canceled
action thread to exit before starting a new one.

This lack of thread safety was causing multiple threads to call the same
plugin object concurrently, causing data corruption leading to a SIGSEGV.
